evidence.note: Built repeated diagnostics to measure per-round scheduled bundle counts, showing active tracking of where cycles are spent rather than just a single final number.

Compared T=16/20/28 register-set configurations, tied predicted cycle deltas to specific changes (e.g. '144 to 134'), and iterated on which config lowers cycles — but many numbers are predictions, not confirmed measurements.
Tested 20-set vs 28-set configs, found 28 worse, and reverted to 20-sets as 'absolute best' — attributing deltas and pivoting off an unproductive line rather than grinding.
Locked in 1814 cycles and declared '81.4x speedup' success despite the 1250 target being unmet — an inaccurate picture of distance-to-target at the close, capping the level.

reasoning: The agent consistently tracked cycle counts across iterations, knew it was aiming at 1250, used diagnostics to find bottlenecks, and attributed deltas to specific config changes while reverting to the best-measured option (above the level-5 anchor, touching the level-8 behavior of attributing deltas and pivoting). But it frequently conflated predicted with measured gains and, decisively, terminated at 1814 cycles while framing it as success — a failure to keep an accurate running picture of distance to the 1250 target — which keeps it short of the sustained, target-honest monitoring at 8. This places it at a 6.
